subject: Status: Pokec repro matches, internal logs bind harder
body:
Status.

The port compiles clean under C++17 and the oracle interfaces (SubmodularFunction / Matroid subclasses) mapped onto our retrieval scoring with less than a day of glue.

Repro: on Pokec maximum coverage we match the paper's pattern — the fair streaming algorithm gives up single-digit-percent coverage versus unconstrained greedy while satisfying the per-group constraints exactly; our runs land within noise of the reference implementation.

Internal-logs pilot (Fumiko): early replays show the fairness constraint binds much harder on our data than on Pokec — group skew is worse — so the utility cost is closer to 8-9% on some surfaces. That's the number product will care about; we should present it per-surface, not averaged.

Risk: partition-matroid config per surface is manual right now. Freya's config-generation tool is the fix but adds a week.

Umar
